title: Cross-layer telemetry contracts for routing & fallback flows
content:
Purpose
This is a working playbook for defining lightweight, cross-layer telemetry contracts that explicitly cover request routing, model variant fallbacks, and regional failover paths in the Redwood inference stack. The goal: give engineers a minimal, actionable spec that both runtimes and routing services can implement to make dashboards, SLOs, and incident triage deterministic across fallthrough paths.

Motivation
- We currently have divergent signal shapes when a request is routed to a cheaper model or a fallback region (metrics use different names, spans miss trace anchors). That makes root-cause analysis slow and dashboards noisy.
- Need a small set of required fields and conventions so queries and alerts behave consistently regardless of which model/region handled a request.

Audience
- Runtime engineers (serving-runtime)
- Router & smart-routing teams (platform-engineering)
- Observability & SREs
- Product teams running rollouts/dark launches

High-level contract (must-haves)
1) Per-request context tags (attach to metric events and traces):
   - request_id (string): unique request id generated at API ingress.
   - routing_decision (string enum): original_model | model_variant | capacity_tier | region_fallback | quota_fallback | degraded_path
   - final_model (string): model identifier used to serve tokens (e.g., redwood/gpt-13b-q4_8bit).
   - model_family (string): coarse family for aggregation (e.g., gpt-13b).
   - region (string): region code of execution (e.g., us-west1).
   - tenant_id (string) optional: tenant identifier for multi-tenant dashboards (PII policy below).

2) Trace span conventions (name, attributes):
   - Ingress span (span.kind=server) name="api.ingress" attributes: request_id, route_policy_id, decision_time_ms.
   - Router span name="router.decision" attributes: routing_decision, candidate_models (list pseudo-string), selected_model, routing_err_code (if any).
   - Serve span name="runtime.serve" attributes: final_model, model_version, gpu_type, kv_cache_hit (bool), batch_size, seq_len.
   - Fallback span name="router.fallback" present when routing_decision != original_model. Include fallback_reason and original_model_hint.
   - End-to-end span should be parented under api.ingress so traces can stitch across services.

3) Metric naming and minimal labels (prefer snake_case):
   - inference.latency.p50/p95/p99 (ms) labels: final_model, region, tenant_hash (see privacy), routing_decision.
   - inference.tokens.generated.count labels: final_model, region, tenant_hash, routing_decision.
   - inference.kv_cache.hit_rate labels: final_model, region.
   - routing.fallback.count labels: fallback_reason, original_model, selected_model, region.
   - routing.decision.latency.ms labels: route_policy_id, region.

4) Sampling & retention rules for traces
   - Default trace sample 1% for normal requests.
   - Always sample traces where routing_decision != original_model (100%).
   - Always sample traces where latency > p99 baseline for that model_family (100%).
   - For tenant-owned SRE escalations, provide on-demand increased sampling via probe flags.

5) Privacy and cardinality constraints
   - Do NOT include raw prompt text in attributes. Traces may include a prompt_hash (sha256) and truncated prompt_signature tokens if required by the owning product.
   - tenant_id must be hashed to tenant_hash (first 8 chars of sha256) before emission to global metrics backends.
   - Candidate_models as a list should be limited to first 5 entries to avoid high-cardinality.

Dashboard guidance (templates & notes)
- Routing overview panel (for SRE & platform): stacked bar of routing.fallback.count by fallback_reason over time + heatmap of region vs final_model. Widgets:
  - time series: routing.fallback.count{region=*} / 1m
  - heatmap: count by region x routing_decision (use top 10 models).
- Latency guardrail panels (for product owners): latency percentiles of inference.latency.* split by routing_decision (original vs fallback).
- Model economics widget (for product & infra): cost_estimate_per_1000_tokens = sum(tokens * model_unit_cost) with routing_decision breakdown. Use exported tag final_model and routing_decision.
- Triaging shortcut panel: top 20 request_id traces where routing.fallback.count increased combined with inference.latency.p99 exceedance. Link to trace viewer using request_id.

Runbook snippets (short)
- Alert: routing.fallback.count spikes > 5x baseline for > 5m
  - Pager: SRE oncall, alert to #observability, run routing.policy-health playbook (linked).
  - Quick check: are router.decision.latency.ms elevated? Check router.decision traces for route_policy_id.
  - If final_model shows high error rates, roll back policy to previous stable policy id via rollout console.

- Alert: inference.latency.p99 for model_family > threshold
  - Capture 5 traces sampled above threshold (should be auto-sampled).
  - Correlate kv_cache_hit false rates and batch_size drops.

Integration checklist for teams (minimal implementation)
- [ ] router: emit router.decision span and routing_decision attribute + route_policy_id.
- [ ] runtime: ensure runtime.serve span includes final_model and kv_cache_hit attribute.
- [ ] api gateway: attach request_id and start api.ingress span.
- [ ] metrics infra: expose inference.latency.* and routing.fallback.count with required labels.
- [ ] dashboards: add routing overview and triage panel.
- [ ] alerting: create SLO tied to percent of requests hitting original_model during canary windows.

Open questions / discussion items (for eng sync)
- How deterministic should routing_decision enums be? (Proposal: small fixed set with clear semantics; extend with routing_flags for experiments.)
- Do we want an explicit policy_version label on metrics or rely only on route_policy_id? Policy_version might simplify rollout queries.
- Can the payment of adding three attributes (request_id, routing_decision, final_model) be standardized as a lightweight SDK helper for all services?

Operational notes / cost tradeoffs
- Sampling 100% of fallback traces will increase trace storage; mitigated because fallback fraction is normally <1%. Estimate: if fallback rate spikes to 5% at peak, increase in traces ~5x for that period. Budget for these bursts in trace retention.
- Limit candidate_models list and model names to canonical short ids to avoid exploding label cardinality. Maintain a model_aliases map in confluence (linked) that instruments should reference.

Next steps (owners)
- Aisha: draft lightweight SDK helper and sample code snippets for api gateway and runtime instrumentation (due 2024-11-01).
- Miguel: prototype a triage dashboard and heatmap in the observability sandbox (due 2024-11-08).
- Jonah: update routing service to emit route_policy_id and ensure parent/child spans (due 2024-11-15).

Notes to reviewers
- This doc is intentionally short and prescriptive. It should be usable by runtime/route teams with minimal friction. Add comments inline or annotate in the linked Confluence page for longer-running decisions.

Raw snippets (for copy/paste)
- metric: inference.latency.p95{final_model="%s",region="%s",routing_decision="%s"}
- trace span naming: "api.ingress" -> "router.decision" -> "runtime.serve" -> optional "router.fallback"

References
- Confluence: OBS-telemetry-contracts (detailed rationale)
- GitHub PR: telemetry-instrumentation/pull/87 (SDK helper PoC)
- Jira: OBS-4213 (dashboard work item)

Changelog
- 2024-10-18 initial draft (Aisha)
- 2024-11-02 added sampling rules and dashboard widget sketches (Miguel)
- 2025-01-12 clarified tenant_hash rules and ownership notes (Evelyn)

- add sample Grafana panels JSON export

End of doc
